chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from the one who told him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about 'Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim', so he said:

The Baa' is the Magnificence of Allah, the Seen is the Sublimity of Allah, and the Miim is the Kingdom of Allah. He said: I said: Allah? He said: The Alif is the Bounties of Allah upon His creation from the bliss of our Divine Authority, and the Laam is the Binding of Allah for His creation to our Divine Authority. I said: And the Haa'? Then he said: Ignominy to he who opposes Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, upon whom are Allah's blessings. I said: The Rahmaan? He said: (The Merciful) With all the world. I said: The Raheem? He said: (The Merciful) With the believers in particular.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of the letters in Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a unique Isma'ili-style exegesis where the letters of 'Bismillah' are decoded as divine attributes, notably linking the Alif and Lam to the 'Ala' (blessings) and 'Ilzam' (binding authority) of the Ahl al-Bayt. This interpretation underscores the centrality of Wilayah in Shia theology by grounding the opening of the Quran in the spiritual authority of the Imams. The distinction between Rahman (universal mercy) and Rahim (specific mercy) further highlights the dual scope of divine grace in Shia cosmology.
